title: Console rapid surface indexing: compact switcher & route map
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: as Console surfaces grow (dashboards, rollouts, cost views, model routes), customers spend too many clicks and time re-orienting between contexts. Current sidebar is deep and visually noisy; workspace switching resets context and hides frequently-accessed routes. Goal: design a compact, index-driven navigation pattern ("surface indexing") that surfaces key entry points, preserves workspace context, and gives a small-footprint compact switcher for fast route jumping.

Scope: desktop + large tablet (priority), keyboard-first interactions, accessibility compliance (ARIA), prototype for engineering handoff. Exclude mobile re-skin in this ticket (follow-up).

Approach: build a two-layer pattern: (1) Compact index: flattened, searchable list of console surfaces with micro-metadata (type badge, last-used timestamp, pinned flag); (2) Context strip: persistent chips that show current workspace/route context and allow sticky routes across switches. Combine with a visual route-map preview on hover (mini-map showing nested pages) to reduce lost navigation.

Success metrics: reduce median time-to-target route by 30% for power users, reduce average clicks to core dashboard from onboarding default by 40%, increase keyboard navigation adoption by 25% in pilot orgs.

Constraints & trade-offs: avoid duplicating the top nav—we keep a single source of truth for routes in the router config (ENG dependency). Prototype should avoid heavy new icons set; use existing token palette. Kinesthetic users must be supported (keyboard + mouse).

Deliverables: Figma prototype with interactions, list of route metadata required by backend, accessibility spec, usability test results, engineering handoff doc with acceptance criteria and feature flag gating.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates compact switcher, index search, hover route-map, and context strip interactions
6 moderated usability sessions with target user personas (Platform Engineers, Product Managers, Devs) and summary notes > 60% success rate on first-try route discovery
Design tokens and accessible color contrast documented; ARIA roles specified for index and chips
Engineering ticket created with route mapping, API contract for last-used/pinned metadata, and keyboard bindings (ENG-78321)
Feature rollout plan with canary flag and instrumentation events for analytics (time_to_route, clicks_to_route, search_queries)
Prototype includes edge case flows: multi-tenant workspace switch with preserved query params, mobile fallback messaging
